summary: This informational memo from Toshiba describes an internetworking architecture meant to make better use of the properties of ATM networks. It is a vendor proposal rather than an Internet standard.

eli5.summary: A company explains its idea for a shortcut road that skips most traffic lights.

questions: what is cell switch router csr
how does atm routing work with ip
what are bypass pipes in atm
subtitle: A router architecture that combines IP forwarding with ATM cell switching for high-throughput, low-latency networking.

tldr.problem: Standard IP routers process every packet at each hop, creating latency and throughput limits; ATM offers speed but bypasses routers entirely, breaking IP's subnet model.
tldr.mechanism: A Cell Switch Router (CSR) adds ATM cell-switching capabilities to conventional routers, allowing specific IP flows to bypass router processing via ATM Bypass-pipes while maintaining standard IP routing for other traffic.
tldr.outcome: The architecture enables high-bandwidth, low-latency paths for applications that need them while preserving standard IP routing, and provides a foundation for integrating IP-level resource reservation with ATM switching.

facts.label: Bypass function
facts.value: Concatenated ATM paths for IP flows

today: RFC 2098 is Informational and not obsoleted. While the specific CSR architecture did not see widespread deployment, its core concepts of hybrid IP-ATM forwarding influenced later architectures. Today, MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching) provides similar functionality with better standardization and wider adoption.

sections.title: The Cell Switch Router Concept
sections.content:
This RFC describes a new internetworking architecture from Toshiba that makes better use of ATM technology while preserving the router-based IP concept. The key innovation is the Cell Switch Router (CSR), a device that combines conventional IP datagram forwarding with ATM cell-switching capabilities.

Traditional approaches either use Classical IP to run IP over ATM (but still process at each router hop) or use NHRP to create direct ATM connections across subnets (but require complex next-hop resolution). The CSR approach offers a middle path: it creates direct ATM paths for traffic that benefits from them while maintaining IP routing for everything else.
sections.eli5: A CSR is like a super-smart router that can either check your packet like a normal router, or send it straight through an ATM fast lane if you are in a hurry.

sections.title: Architecture and Default Circuits
sections.content:
The CSR architecture defines two types of ATM virtual circuits. The Default-VC is a general-purpose circuit used by any communication selecting standard hop-by-hop IP routing. All cells received on this VC are assembled to IP datagrams and handled based on their IP headers.

The Dedicated-VC is used by specific IP flows and can be concatenated with other Dedicated-VCs to form an ATM Bypass-pipe. This bypass-pipe carries cells that belong to specific flows (identified by destination IP, source/destination IP pairs, ports, or IPv6 flow labels) directly between router nodes without datagram assembly and IP processing at intermediate hops.
sections.eli5: Default-VC is like the regular checkpoints where every car stops, and Dedicated-VC is the express lane where cars with matching tickets can flow through without stopping.

sections.title: How Bypass-Pipes Work
sections.content:
When a bypass-pipe is established, a CSR checks the VPI/VCI value of each incoming cell. If a mapping from input interface/VPI/VCI to output interface/VPI/VCI is found in the ATM routing table, the cell is forwarded directly through the ATM switch module. If the mapping is not found or the table indicates an IP module as output, the cell is assembled to an IP datagram and forwarded based on IP routing.

Routes for bypass-pipes follow IP routing information in each CSR, ensuring consistency with IP-level routing decisions. However, the actual ATM-level paths for the individual virtual circuits are determined by ATM routing protocols such as PNNI, and can differ from IP routing. Bypass-pipes can be established from host to host, router to host, host to router, or router to router.
sections.eli5: The CSR checks each cell: if it is part of a fast flow with a reserved fast lane, it goes straight through; otherwise, it gets unpacked and forwarded the normal way.

sections.title: Control and Management Strategies
sections.content:
The RFC discusses multiple control architectures for managing bypass-pipes. The primary decisions are how to provide Dedicated-VCs (on-demand setup, pre-allocated pools, or VCI allocation within PVPs), how to convey control messages (inband on the data VCs, outband on separate VCs, or via ATM signaling), and whether control should be distributed to all nodes or centralized at cloud boundaries.

Additional considerations include upstream vs. downstream initiation of circuit setup, and whether state management is hard-state (explicit release messages) or soft-state (periodic refresh). Each combination offers different tradeoffs in setup time, resource efficiency, and operational complexity.
sections.eli5: There are many ways to organize who asks for a fast lane, when they ask, and how the request travels through the network, each with different pros and cons.

sections.title: Integration with IP Resource Reservation
sections.content:
A key advantage of the CSR architecture is its compatibility with IP-level resource reservation protocols like RSVP. Unlike NHRP which assumes hard-state sender-oriented control, CSRs can handle RSVP's soft-state, receiver-oriented approach. When RSVP messages traverse a CSR network requesting specific bandwidth and QoS, the CSRs can establish bypass-pipes that satisfy those requirements through cooperation between RSVP and the bypass-pipe control protocol.

The architecture also naturally supports multicast IP flows without requiring modifications to IP multicast over ATM or multicast routing techniques, since CSRs maintain subnet-by-subnet internetworking for control protocols. This unified approach bridges IP and ATM technologies in a flexible framework.
sections.eli5: When an application asks for a fast, guaranteed lane using RSVP, the CSR can automatically set up that fast path through ATM without special tricks.
